> The important constraint is that `.asv-openmp/*` is git-ignored and the results are machine-specific. GitHub Actions cannot regenerate this exact report unless the benchmark result JSON is also uploaded or committed, so the cleanest approach for this report is a dedicated `gh-pages` branch containing only the generated HTML, updated from the machine that ran the benchmarks.

Yes. The generated report is a self-contained static HTML file, so GitHub Pages can serve it directly.

Because `.asv-openmp/` is intentionally ignored and contains machine-specific results, I recommend publishing the HTML from a dedicated `gh-pages` branch. This keeps generated benchmark output separate from the source code.

**First Deployment**

Run from the `GSTools` repository:

```bash
cd /Users/lealroja/Documents/UFZ/MPS-Tools/GSTools

git worktree add --orphan -b gh-pages /tmp/gstools-gh-pages

cp .asv-openmp/case-backend-comparison.html \
  /tmp/gstools-gh-pages/index.html

touch /tmp/gstools-gh-pages/.nojekyll

git -C /tmp/gstools-gh-pages add index.html .nojekyll
git -C /tmp/gstools-gh-pages commit -m "Publish benchmark comparison report"
git -C /tmp/gstools-gh-pages push -u origin gh-pages

git worktree remove /tmp/gstools-gh-pages
```

Then configure GitHub:

1. Open the repository on GitHub.
2. Go to **Settings → Pages**.
3. Under **Build and deployment**, select **Deploy from a branch**.
4. Select branch `gh-pages` and folder `/(root)`.
5. Click **Save**.

For your `origin` fork, the report URL should be:

```text
https://jeilealr.github.io/GSTools/
```

**Updating the Report**

After rerunning the benchmarks and regenerating the HTML:

```bash
git worktree add /tmp/gstools-gh-pages gh-pages

cp .asv-openmp/case-backend-comparison.html \
  /tmp/gstools-gh-pages/index.html

git -C /tmp/gstools-gh-pages add index.html
git -C /tmp/gstools-gh-pages commit -m "Update benchmark comparison report"
git -C /tmp/gstools-gh-pages push

git worktree remove /tmp/gstools-gh-pages
```

Your existing benchmark CI only performs smoke checks, so it cannot currently regenerate this full report. Publishing from the machine that ran the benchmarks avoids mixing performance results from different GitHub-hosted runners.

GitHub documentation: [Configuring a publishing source](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/configuring-a-publishing-source-for-your-github-pages-site).

> The live examples confirm this is a common ASV pattern. One project uses a separate Pages repository, while others publish generated files directly to a `gh-pages` branch; your single self-contained report is simpler than either setup.
</details>

Yes. Publishing benchmark dashboards as static GitHub Pages sites is an established ASV workflow.

**Real Examples**
- [Official ASV example dashboard](https://pv.github.io/numpy-bench/)
  Published from the repository’s [`gh-pages` branch](https://github.com/pv/numpy-bench/tree/gh-pages).

- [sgkit benchmark dashboard](https://sgkit-dev.github.io/sgkit-benchmarks-asv/)
  The generated website is stored in the [`sgkit-benchmarks-asv` repository](https://github.com/sgkit-dev/sgkit-benchmarks-asv).
  Their [GitHub Actions workflow](https://github.com/sgkit-dev/sgkit/blob/main/.github/workflows/benchmark.yml) runs:
  ```bash
  asv run
  asv publish
  ```
  It then pushes the generated HTML to the Pages repository.

- [Physipy benchmark dashboard](https://mocquin.github.io/physipy/)
  Published directly from its [`gh-pages` branch](https://github.com/mocquin/physipy/tree/gh-pages).

- [Pandas performance dashboard](https://speed.pandas.pydata.org/)
  A larger production ASV dashboard using the same static-site concept.

**How Your Page Will Look**

GitHub Pages does not add GitHub menus or modify the HTML. It serves your generated file unchanged.

Your deployed page will look exactly like your current [case-backend-comparison.html](./GSTools/.asv-openmp/case-backend-comparison.html), including:

- GSTools backend comparison title
- Metric, benchmark, case, thread, commit, and backend filters
- Cython versus Rust bar charts
- Benchmark trend plots

If published as `index.html`, its URL would be:

```text
https://jeilealr.github.io/GSTools/
```

If published with its current filename:

```text
https://jeilealr.github.io/GSTools/case-backend-comparison.html
```

ASV officially supports this workflow through [`asv gh-pages`](https://asv.readthedocs.io/en/stable/using.html#viewing-the-results). However, because your report is a custom standalone HTML file rather than the default ASV dashboard, publishing it as `index.html` on the `gh-pages` branch remains the simplest approach.

> I’ll inspect how the repository currently installs optional dependencies and how ASV expands install commands, then I’ll recommend the simplest single-source approach that works in both GitHub Actions and ASV environments.
</details>

Yes, `pyproject.toml` should ideally be the single source of truth:

```toml
rust = ["gstools_core>=1.3.0"]
```

However, directly using:

```bash
pip install '.[rust]'
```

inside ASV is risky because it also installs GSTools’ normal dependencies and could override versions selected by the ASV matrix.

The cleanest approach is a small helper that reads the Rust extra from `pyproject.toml` and installs it:

```python
# benchmarks/tools/install_extra.py
import subprocess
import sys
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

extra = sys.argv[1]
config = tomllib.loads(Path("pyproject.toml").read_text())
requirements = config["project"]["optional-dependencies"][extra]

subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", *requirements])
```

Then everywhere use:

```bash
python benchmarks/tools/install_extra.py rust
```

And in ASV:

```json
"install_command": [
  "in-dir={env_dir} python {conf_dir}/benchmarks/tools/install_extra.py rust",
  "in-dir={env_dir} python -m pip install --no-deps {build_dir}"
]
```

This avoids manually synchronizing:

- `pyproject.toml`
- `asv.conf.json`
- `asv.openmp.conf.json`
- GitHub Actions
- documentation

Using the helper is slightly more setup now, but is better than maintaining the version manually in four places. `pip install '.[rust]'` is simpler, but I would not use it for ASV because it weakens dependency-version control.

> The key distinction is between a **PR comparison** and a **long-term main-branch history**. ASV does not rerun every historical commit automatically; your current `main~5..main` command explicitly asks it to rerun five commits each time. For PRs, the scalable unit is only the PR base and PR head; for the public history, it is only the newly merged `main` commit.
>
> Your custom report is a reasonable primary site. The current five-commit result store is about 80 KB and the self-contained report about 412 KB, so storage is not the immediate concern. The larger concern is trustworthy measurements: `ubuntu-latest` hardware can change, and PR-only results cannot always be reused after squash/rebase merges because the final commit differs. I need to lock three policy choices before producing the implementation plan.
>
> That gives a coherent split: preserve the existing cross-platform availability checks, add a full Linux comparison job only for PRs, and maintain the public accepted-history with one benchmark of each newly merged `main` commit.
>
> I’m checking the current workflow and report interfaces now so the plan can specify exact triggers, refs, persistence, and publication behavior. The remaining design issue is where cumulative ASV result JSON lives; GitHub Pages deployment artifacts are temporary, so the accepted history needs a durable branch or another store.
>
> The durable source of truth should be a dedicated branch in the same repository, with generated Pages content at its root and cumulative ASV JSON alongside it. That avoids relying on Actions caches or temporary artifacts and avoids cross-repository credentials.
>
> I’m also validating whether `asv continuous` fits the PR comparison cleanly. If it does, the PR job can benchmark exactly base SHA versus head SHA and produce a comparison without inventing a moving five-commit window.
>
> `asv continuous BASE HEAD` is the right PR command: it is specifically designed for CI, runs the two revisions side by side, supports your benchmark filter and `--show-stderr`, and records the results needed by the custom report. The accepted-history job should instead run only `MAIN_SHA^!` with `--skip-existing-successful`.
>
> For scale, I recommend retaining every accepted result JSON, while limiting the custom interactive page to a recent window and leaving the complete trend history in native ASV under `/asv/`. This keeps the richer report responsive without deleting historical data. One repository/ownership decision remains especially important because PR workflows execute in the repository receiving the PR, not automatically in your fork.
>
> A dedicated benchmark-results repository is a strong long-term option, but it changes the trust and credential model. The code and PR workflow stay in `jeilealr/GSTools`; the trusted post-merge job must write results/site to `jeilealr/<benchmark-repo>` using a GitHub App or fine-grained token because `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write across repositories.

name: Install dependencies\n        run: |\n          sudo apt update -y\n          python -m pip install --upgrade pip\n          pip install asv\n\n      - name: Set and log asv machine configuration\n        run: |\n          asv machine --yes --config benchmarks/asv.conf.json\n          echo \"Machine Configuration:\"\n          cat ~/.asv-machine.json\n          rm ~/.asv-machine.json\n\n          echo \"Setting machine name to $MACHINE_NAME\"\n          asv machine --machine $MACHINE_NAME --yes --config $ASV_CONFIG -v\n\n      - > The `sgkit` model matches your use case well. Their source repository runs ASV on `main`, clones a separate `sgkit-benchmarks-asv` repository, merges the previous result JSON, regenerates the site, and pushes it. That benchmark repository’s `main` branch is both durable storage and the GitHub Pages source.
>
> For your fork, I recommend adopting that model now as `jeilealr/gstools-benchmarks-asv`, with a cleaner site layout: custom report at `/`, complete native ASV at `/asv/`, and cumulative raw JSON at `/results/`. A fine-grained token restricted to only that benchmark repository is the practical authentication choice for your personal fork; later, upstream should replace it with an organization-owned GitHub App or organization secret.
>
> The architecture is now fixed: PR runs compare base versus head and upload both reports; accepted `main` commits are appended to a dedicated public benchmark repository, which serves the custom recent-50 view and complete native ASV history.
>
> I’m doing one final feasibility pass around repository creation, Pages setup, machine metadata, and test coverage. The only unavoidable manual prerequisite should be creating the restricted token and adding it as a secret, because workflows cannot securely create their own cross-repository credential.

> One important configuration mismatch remains: the current smoke workflow uses Python 3.14, but `asv.openmp.conf.json` still creates Python 3.12 benchmark environments. For a useful long-term history, the benchmark Python version must be explicitly pinned; a moving `python-latest` value would create discontinuities and is not an ASV config value.
>
> I’m also checking `asv continuous` exit semantics so the required PR check fails only when the benchmark cannot run, unless you explicitly choose to make regressions block merges.
>
> `asv continuous` has one behavior that is wrong for your selected policy: it exits nonzero when performance worsens beyond its factor, which would silently turn the required check into a regression gate. The PR job should therefore use `asv run HASHFILE:<base-and-head>` with interleaved rounds, then run `asv compare` only for informational output. Benchmark/install/report failures still block the PR, but a measured slowdown does not.
>
> The dedicated repository does not exist yet. It will need to be created as public, Pages enabled from `main`/root, and a restricted token added to `jeilealr/GSTools` as `BENCHMARKS_REPO_TOKEN`. One final version choice remains.
>
> Yes. I’ll include the exact GitHub UI steps and the minimum permissions, including how to verify the secret without exposing it. I’m checking GitHub’s current fine-grained token and Actions-secret interfaces so the instructions match the current settings pages.
>

> The token setup will be an explicit guided checkpoint, not something left as an assumption. I can prepare everything around it, but you must generate and paste the token yourself because GitHub shows it only once and it must never appear in chat, source files, or logs.
>
> The minimum token scope is narrow: access only `jeilealr/gstools-benchmarks-asv`, with repository permission `Contents: Read and write`; all other configurable permissions remain `No access`. The secret belongs in `jeilealr/GSTools`, because that is where the publishing workflow runs.
>
> There is one interaction worth fixing before the final plan: GitHub-required checks and workflow path filters can leave a PR blocked when the workflow is skipped. The clean design is to trigger the workflow for every PR, detect changed paths inside it, run the expensive full benchmark only for performance-relevant changes, and expose one always-completing required gate job.
>
> That avoids spending hours benchmarking documentation-only PRs while still giving branch protection a reliable required check.
>

>
> # OpenMP Benchmark CI and Publishing
>
> ## Summary
>
> - Use Python 3.14 in both `asv.conf.json` and `asv.openmp.conf.json`.
> - Preserve existing cross-platform smoke/readiness checks.
> - Add required Linux PR benchmarks comparing only base and head commits.
> - Publish accepted `main` history to `jeilealr/gstools-benchmarks-asv`.
>
> ## Implementation
>
> - Change both ASV configurations from:

> {"content": "import * as core from '@actions/core'\nimport * as fsHelper from './fs-helper'\nimport * as gitAuthHelper from './git-auth-helper'\nimport * as gitCommandManager from './git-command-manager'\nimport * as gitDirectoryHelper from './git-directory-helper'\nimport * as githubApiHelper from './github-api-helper'\nimport * as io from '@actions/io'\nimport * as path from 'path'\nimport * as refHelper from './ref-helper'\nimport * as stateHelper from './state-helper'\nimport * as urlHelper from './url-helper'\nimport {\n  MinimumGitSparseCheckoutVersion,\n  IGitCommandManager\n} from './git-command-manager'\nimport {IGitSourceSettings} from './git-source-settings'\n\nexport async function getSource(settings: IGitSourceSettings): Promise<void> {\n  // Repository URL\n  core.info(\n    `Syncing repository: ${settings.repositoryOwner}/${settings.repositoryName}`\n  )\n  const repositoryUrl = urlHelper.getFetchUrl(settings)\n\n  // Remove conflicting file path\n  if (fsHelper.fileExistsSync(settings.repositoryPath)) {\n    await io.rmRF(settings.repositoryPath)\n  }\n\n  // Create directory\n  let isExisting = true\n  if (!fsHelper.directoryExistsSync(settings.repositoryPath)) {\n    isExisting = false\n    await io.mkdirP(settings.repositoryPath)\n  }\n\n  // Git command manager\n  core.startGroup('Getting Git version info')\n  const git = await getGitCommandManager(settings)\n  core.endGroup()\n\n  let authHelper: gitAuthHelper.IGitAuthHelper | null = null\n  try {\n    if (git) {\n      authHelper = gitAuthHelper.createAuthHelper(git, settings)\n      if (settings.setSafeDirectory) {\n        // Setup the repository path as a safe directory, so if we pass this into a container job with a different user it doesn't fail\n        // Otherwise all git commands we run in a container fail\n        await authHelper.configureTempGlobalConfig()\n        core.info(\n          `Adding repository directory to the temporary git global config as a safe directory`\n        )\n\n        await git\n          .config('safe.directory', settings.repositoryPath, true, true)\n          .catch(error => {\n            core.info(\n              `Failed to initialize safe directory with error: ${error}`\n            )\n          })\n\n        stateHelper.setSafeDirectory()\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Prepare existing directory, otherwise recreate\n    if (isExisting) {\n      await gitDirectoryHelper.prepareExistingDirectory(\n        git,\n        settings.repositoryPath,\n        repositoryUrl,\n        settings.clean,\n        settings.ref\n      )\n    }\n\n    if (!git) {\n      // Downloading using REST API\n      core.info(`The repository will be downloaded using the GitHub REST API`)\n      core.info(\n        `To create a local Git repository instead, add Git ${gitCommandManager.MinimumGitVersion} or higher to the PATH`\n      )\n      if (settings.submodules) {\n        throw new Error(\n          `Input 'submodules' not supported when falling back to download using the GitHub REST API. To create a local Git repository instead, add Git ${gitCommandManager.MinimumGitVersion} or higher to the PATH.`\n        )\n      } else if (settings.sshKey) {\n        throw new Error(\n          `Input 'ssh-key' not supported when falling back to download using the GitHub REST API. To create a local Git repository instead, add Git ${gitCommandManager.MinimumGitVersion} or higher to the PATH.`\n        )\n      }\n\n      await githubApiHelper.downloadRepository(\n        settings.authToken,\n        settings.repositoryOwner,\n        settings.repositoryName,\n        settings.ref,\n        settings.commit,\n        settings.repositoryPath,\n        settings.githubServerUrl\n      )\n      return\n    }\n\n    // Save state for POST action\n    stateHelper.setRepositoryPath(settings.repositoryPath)\n\n    // Initialize the repository\n    if (\n      !fsHelper.directoryExistsSync(path.join(settings.repositoryPath, '.git'))\n    ) {\n      core.startGroup('Determining repository object format')\n      const objectFormatResult =\n        await githubApiHelper.tryGetRepositoryObjectFormat(\n          settings.authToken,\n          settings.repositoryOwner,\n          settings.repositoryName,\n          settings.githubServerUrl,\n          settings.commit\n        )\n      const objectFormat = objectFormatResult.succeeded\n        ? objectFormatResult.format\n        : ''\n      if (objectFormat === 'sha256') {\n        core.info('Detected SHA-256 repository object format')\n      }\n      core.endGroup()\n\n      core.startGroup('Initializing the repository')\n      await git.init(objectFormat)\n      await git.remoteAdd('origin', repositoryUrl)\n      core.endGroup()\n    }\n\n    // Disable automatic garbage collection\n    core.startGroup('Disabling automatic garbage collection')\n    if (!(await git.tryDisableAutomaticGarbageCollection())) {\n      core.warning(\n        `Unable to turn off git automatic garbage collection. The git fetch operation may trigger garbage collection and cause a delay.`\n      )\n    }\n    core.endGroup()\n\n    // If we didn't initialize it above, do it now\n    if (!authHelper) {\n      authHelper = gitAuthHelper.createAuthHelper(git, settings)\n    }\n    // Configure auth\n    core.startGroup('Setting up auth')\n    await authHelper.configureAuth()\n    core.endGroup()\n\n    // Determine the default branch\n    if (!settings.ref && !settings.commit) {\n      core.startGroup('Determining the default branch')\n      if (settings.sshKey) {\n        settings.ref = await git.getDefaultBranch(repositoryUrl)\n      } else {\n        settings.ref = await githubApiHelper.getDefaultBranch(\n          settings.authToken,\n          settings.repositoryOwner,\n          settings.repositoryName,\n          settings.githubServerUrl\n        )\n      }\n      core.endGroup()\n    }\n\n    // LFS install\n    if (settings.lfs) {\n      await git.lfsInstall()\n    }\n\n    // Fetch\n    core.startGroup('Fetching the repository')\n    const fetchOptions: {\n      filter?: string\n      fetchDepth?: number\n      showProgress?: boolean\n    } = {}\n\n    if (settings.filter) {\n      fetchOptions.filter = settings.filter\n    } else if (settings.sparseCheckout) {\n      fetchOptions.filter = 'blob:none'\n    }\n\n    if (settings.fetchDepth <= 0) {\n      // Fetch all branches and tags\n      let refSpec = refHelper.getRefSpecForAllHistory(\n        settings.ref,\n        settings.commit\n      )\n      await git.fetch(refSpec, fetchOptions)\n\n      // When all history is fetched, the ref we're interested in may have moved to a different\n      // commit (push or force push). If so, fetch again with a targeted refspec.\n      if (!(await refHelper.testRef(git, settings.ref, settings.commit))) {\n        refSpec = refHelper.getRefSpec(settings.ref, settings.commit)\n        await git.fetch(refSpec, fetchOptions)\n\n        // Verify the ref now matches. For branches, the targeted fetch above brings\n        // in the specific commit. Yes. A PR from `benchmarking` into **your fork’s `main`** is the correct end-to-end staging test before involving `GeoStat-Framework/GSTools`.

**Current State**

- Token permissions are correct: only `gstools-benchmarks-asv`, with `Contents: Read and write`.
- Secret name `BENCHMARKS_REPO_TOKEN` matches the workflow.
- `gstools-benchmarks-asv` still has zero commits and no actual `main` branch.
- Your new workflow/configuration changes are currently uncommitted locally and are not yet on `origin/benchmarking`.
- Your fork’s `main` is behind `upstream/main`.

**Recommended Test Sequence**

1. Initialize the benchmark repository.

   Create an initial `README.md` commit in:

   https://github.com/jeilealr/gstools-benchmarks-asv

   Then return to Pages settings, select `main` and `/(root)`, and click **Save**. The publisher’s checkout step requires an existing branch.

2. Sync your fork’s `main` with `GeoStat-Framework/GSTools:main`.

   Use GitHub’s **Sync fork** button. This prevents the test PR from including unrelated upstream synchronization changes.

3. Commit and push the benchmark changes from your local `benchmarking` branch. Exclude the unrelated files `AGENTS.MD` and `direct_sampling_mps_guide.md`.

4. Open the fork-only PR:

   https://github.com/jeilealr/GSTools/compare/main...benchmarking?expand=1

5. Before merging, verify the PR workflow:

   - `Full OpenMP comparison on Linux` runs.
   - `OpenMP benchmark gate` succeeds.
   - Download the `openmp-pr-<number>` artifact.
   - Inspect `index.html`, `asv/`, `results/`, and `comparison.txt`.

   This PR stage does **not** receive or use `BENCHMARKS_REPO_TOKEN`.

6. Merge the PR into your fork’s `main`.

   The trusted `Publish OpenMP Benchmark History` workflow should then:

   - Benchmark the accepted merge commit.
   - Push the generated site into `gstools-benchmarks-asv`.
   - Publish:

   https://jeilealr.github.io/gstools-benchmarks-asv/

7. If publishing fails, the workflow will now exist on `main`, allowing you to rerun it manually through **Actions → Publish OpenMP Benchmark History → Run workflow**.

For the later upstream PR, the publishing job is intentionally skipped because it currently requires `github.repository == 'jeilealr/GSTools'`. The upstream maintainers should decide whether the permanent benchmark repository and deployment credential should belong to `GeoStat-Framework` instead of your personal account.

You have **not created the PR yet**. The Actions run you linked happened before the PR and is not the PR OpenMP test.

## Step 4: Create The PR

On the page shown:

1. Keep:
   - Base: `main`
   - Compare: `benchmarking`
2. Use a title such as:

   `Add OpenMP benchmark CI and publishing`

3. Click **Create pull request**.

Before eventually merging, review the displayed **21 commits / 19 changed files**. This PR contains more than only the new publishing workflow.

## Step 5: Verify The PR Benchmark

After creating the PR:

1. Open the PR’s **Checks** tab.
2. Find **OpenMP PR Benchmark**.
3. Wait for:
   - `Detect benchmark-relevant changes`
   - `Full OpenMP comparison on Linux`
   - `OpenMP benchmark gate`

All three should be green.

### What Is The Artifact?

The artifact is a downloadable ZIP containing the generated benchmark website and results.

To download it:

1. Open the completed **OpenMP PR Benchmark** workflow run.
2. Return to the workflow run’s summary page.
3. Scroll to the bottom to **Artifacts**.
4. Click `openmp-pr-<PR-number>`.

After extracting it, expect:

```text
index.html       custom benchmark report
comparison.txt   ASV base-versus-head comparison
asv/             native ASV website
results/         raw ASV result files
```

Open `index.html` locally to confirm the custom report works. The artifact is only for inspection; it does not publish anything.

## Step 6: Merge Into Your Fork Main

Only after the PR checks and artifact look correct:

1. Click **Merge pull request** in `jeilealr/GSTools`.
2. Confirm the merge.

This changes only your fork’s `main`. It does not affect `GeoStat-Framework/GSTools`.

## Step 7: Verify Publishing

Merging triggers **Publish OpenMP Benchmark History** because it is a trusted push to `jeilealr/GSTools:main`.

Verify:

1. Open [`jeilealr/GSTools` Actions](https://github.com/jeilealr/GSTools/actions).
2. Open **Publish OpenMP Benchmark History**.
3. Wait for it to finish successfully.
4. Confirm files appeared in [`gstools-benchmarks-asv`](https://github.com/jeilealr/gstools-benchmarks-asv).
5. Confirm the website works:

   https://jeilealr.github.io/gstools-benchmarks-asv/

The first publication may take several minutes before GitHub Pages becomes available.

name: Install ASV driver\n+        run: python -m pip install --upgrade pip asv\n+\n+      - name: Configure PR commits and ASV branches\n+        env:\n+          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}\n+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}\n+        run: |\n+          printf '%s\\n%s\\n' \"$BASE_SHA\" \"$HEAD_SHA\" \\\n+            > \"$RUNNER_TEMP/asv-pr-commits.txt\"\n+          python - <<'PY'\n+          import json\n+          import os\n+          from pathlib import Path\n+\n+          config = json.loads(Path(\"asv.openmp.conf.json\").read_text())\n+          config[\"branches\"] = [os.environ[\"BASE_SHA\"], os.environ[\"HEAD_SHA\"]]\n+          Path(\"asv.openmp.pr.conf.json\").write_text(\n+              json.dumps(config, indent=2),\n+              encoding=\"utf8\",\n+          )\n+          PY\n+          echo \"ASV_CONFIG=asv.openmp.pr.conf.json\" >> \"$GITHUB_ENV\"\n+\n+      - name: Configure stable ASV machine name\n+        run: |\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" machine \\\n+            --machine \"$MACHINE_NAME\" \\\n+            --yes\n+\n+      - name: Run full OpenMP comparison\n+        env:\n+          GSTOOLS_BENCHMARK_THREADS: \"1,2,4,8\"\n+        run: |\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" run \\\n+            \"HASHFILE:$RUNNER_TEMP/asv-pr-commits.txt\" \\\n+            --machine \"$MACHINE_NAME\" \\\n+            --interleave-rounds \\\n+            --no-pull \\\n+            --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics \\\n+            --show-stderr\n+\n+      - name: Write informational ASV comparison\n+        env:\n+          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}\n+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}\n+        run: |\n+          mkdir -p .asv-openmp/artifact\n+          set +e\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" compare \\\n+            \"$BASE_SHA\" \\\n+            \"$HEAD_SHA\" \\\n+            --machine \"$MACHINE_NAME\" \\\n+            --split \\\n+            | tee .asv-openmp/artifact/comparison.txt\n+          compare_status=\"${PIPESTATUS[0]}\"\n+          set -e\n+          echo \"ASV comparison exit status: $compare_status\" \\\n+            >> .asv-openmp/artifact/comparison.txt\n+\n+      - name: Build custom and native ASV reports\n+        run: |\n+          python benchmarks/tools/plot_case_backend_comparison.py \\\n+            --results-dir .asv-openmp/results \\\n+            --max-commits 50 \\\n+            --output .asv-openmp/artifact/index.html\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" publish \\\n+            --no-pull \\\n+            --html-dir .asv-openmp/artifact/asv\n+          cp -R .asv-openmp/results .asv-openmp/artifact/results\n+\n+      - benchmark_changes\n+      - benchmark\n+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n+\n+    steps:\n+      - name: Check required benchmark result\n+        env:\n+          CHANGE_RESULT: ${{ needs.benchmark_changes.result }}\n+          BENCHMARK_REQUIRED: ${{ needs.benchmark_changes.outputs.required }}\n+          BENCHMARK_RESULT: ${{ needs.benchmark.result }}\n+        run: |\n+          if [[ \"$CHANGE_RESULT\" != \"success\" ]]; then\n+            echo \"Could not determine whether the benchmark is required.\"\n+            exit 1\n+          fi\n+          if [[ \"$BENCHMARK_REQUIRED\" == \"true\" \\\n+            && \"$BENCHMARK_RESULT\" != \"success\" ]]; then\n+            echo \"The required OpenMP benchmark did not complete successfully.\"\n+            exit 1\n+          fi\n+          if [[ \"$BENCHMARK_REQUIRED\" == \"true\" ]]; then\n+            echo \"The required OpenMP benchmark completed successfully.\"\n+          else\n+            echo \"No benchmark-relevant files changed.\"\n+          fi\n@@ -0,0 +1,118 @@\n+name: Publish OpenMP Benchmark History\n+\n+on:\n+  push:\n+    branches:\n+      - name: Build published reports and preserve raw results\n+        run: |\n+          rm -rf benchmark-site/asv benchmark-site/results\n+          python benchmarks/tools/plot_case_backend_comparison.py \\\n+            --results-dir .asv-openmp/results \\\n+            --max-commits 50 \\\n+            --output benchmark-site/index.html\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" publish \\\n+            --no-pull \\\n+            --html-dir benchmark-site/asv\n+          cp -R .asv-openmp/results benchmark-site/results\n+          touch benchmark-site/.nojekyll\n+\n+      - Airspeed Velocity ([ASV](https://github.com/airspeed-velocity/asv/)) benchmark suite for GSTools and a complementary profiling helper implemented with cProfile (part of the Python standard library).\n+\n+This guide benchmarks GSTools, inspects the\n+results, profiles where runtime is spent, and then decides what to optimize.\n+\n+Unit tests in `tests/` answer \"is the code correct?\". The ASV benchmarks in\n+`benchmarks/` answer \"how fast is this workflow, how much memory does it use,\n+and did that change across commits?\". The complementary cProfile helper\n+answers \"inside this workflow, which Python functions are taking most of the\n+time right now?\".\n+\n+The benchmarks compare two GSTools backends, which gives more context for\n+deciding where optimization work should go:\n+\n+- `cython_fallback`: the default Cython-backed fallback implementation from\n+  [gstools-cython](https://github.com/GeoStat-Framework/GSTools-Cython).\n+- `rust_core`: the Rust-backed implementation from\n+  [gstools_core](https://github.com/GeoStat-Framework/GSTools-Core).\n+\n+## Index\n+\n+- [Setup](#setup)\n+- [Benchmarking Scripts](#benchmarking-scripts)\n+  - [Benchmark Classes](#benchmark-classes)\n+    - [VariogramBenchmarks](#variogrambenchmarks)\n+    - [KrigingBenchmarks](#krigingbenchmarks)\n+    - [RandomFieldBenchmarks](#randomfieldbenchmarks)\n+- [Running The Benchmarks](#running-the-benchmarks)\n+  - [Visualization of Results](#visualization-of-results)\n+    - [Profiling With cProfile](#profiling-with-cprofile)\n+- [Optional Parallelization with OpenMP](#optional-parallelization-with-openmp)\n+  - [OpenMP ASV Configuration](#openmp-asv-configuration)\n+  - [Run on macOS and Linux](#run-on-macos-and-linux)\n+  - [Verify Parallel Backends](#verify-parallel-backends)\n+  - [Automated OpenMP Benchmarking](#automated-openmp-benchmarking)\n+  - [Run on Windows](#run-on-windows)\n+  - [OpenMP Thread Rule](#openmp-thread-rule)\n+  - [HPC Notes](#hpc-notes)\n+  - [Profiling With cProfile for Multiple Threads](#profiling-with-cprofile-for-multiple-threads)\n+- [More ASV Commands](#more-asv-commands)\n+- [External Reference](#external-reference)\n+\n+## Setup\n+\n+The regular installation commands in the main `README.md` install GSTools for\n+normal use. This benchmark guide uses conda because ASV creates isolated\n+benchmark environments for the commits it measures.\n+\n+The default benchmark configuration intentionally compares both backends with\n+one GSTools thread:\n+\n+```text\n+gstools.config.NUM_THREADS = 1\n+```\n+\n+That keeps the first comparison simple: Cython fallback vs Rust core without\n+parallelism as a confounding factor. Parallel/OpenMP scaling is treated as a\n+separate optional experiment because the correct Cython OpenMP build depends on\n+the user's operating system, compiler, and runtime environment.\n+\n+To run the benchmark and the optional cProfile helper, follow these steps (this guide uses Python 3.14):\n+\n+1. Move to the GSTools repository root:\n+\n+```bash\n+cd /path/to/GSTools\n+```\n+\n+2. Create and activate a conda environment for local benchmark work:\n+\n+```bash\n+conda create -n gstools-benchmark -c conda-forge python=3.14 asv\n+conda activate gstools-benchmark\n+```\n+\n+If you already have a suitable conda environment, activate that instead.\n+\n+3. If you use an existing environment, make sure ASV is installed:\n+\n+```bash\n+conda install -c conda-forge asv\n+```\n+\n+4. Create a machine profile once per computer:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv machine --yes\n+```\n+\n+The machine profile records local hardware information so ASV can label\n+results correctly. Do not compare absolute times across different machines.\n+\n+## Benchmarking Scripts\n+\n+The benchmarking setup currently consists of:\n+\n+- `asv.conf.json`: tells ASV how to build GSTools, where benchmarks live, where\n+  to store results, and which Python/environment matrix to use.\n+- `asv.openmp.conf.json`: optional cross-platform ASV configuration that builds\n+  `gstools-cython` from source with OpenMP inside ASV's own environment.\n+- `benchmarks/benchmark_two_point_statistics.py`: contains the ASV benchmark\n+  classes.\n+- `benchmarks/README.md`: this practical guide.\n+- `benchmarks/tools/asv_speedup_summary.py`: reads ASV result JSON files and\n+  prints Rust-vs-Cython speedup ratios or writes a curated Markdown/HTML\n+  report.\n+- `benchmarks/tools/plot_case_backend_comparison.py`: reads ASV result JSON\n+  files and writes a self-contained HTML report with grouped backend bars and\n+  commit trends for selected cases, thread counts, and metrics.\n+- `benchmarks/tools/profile_benchmark_workflows.py`: runs one representative\n+  workflow from `benchmark_two_point_statistics.py` under Python's built-in\n+  `cProfile`, so you can see which functions take time in the current\n+  checkout.\n+- `benchmarks/tools/check_backend_parallel_ready.py`: CI helper that verifies\n+  Cython OpenMP detection and Rust backend execution with more than one\n+  GSTools thread.\n+- `benchmarks/tools/install_pyproject_extras.py`: installs selected optional\n+  dependencies directly from `pyproject.toml` without installing GSTools or\n+  its regular dependencies.\n+- `benchmarks/tools/install_openmp_cython.py`: helper used by\n+  `asv.openmp.conf.json` to compile `gstools-cython` with OpenMP on macOS,\n+  Linux, and native Windows.\n+\n+### ASV Configuration\n+\n+The repo root `asv.conf.json` is tailored to this GSTools checkout:\n+\n+```json\n+{\n+  \"repo\": \".\",\n+  \"branches\": [\"main\"],\n+  \"benchmark_dir\": \"benchmarks\",\n+  \"env_dir\": \".asv/env\",\n+  \"results_dir\": \".asv/results\",\n+  \"html_dir\": \".asv/html\",\n+  \"environment_type\": \"conda\",\n+  \"pythons\": [\"3.14\"],\n+  \"matrix\": {\n+    \"req\": {\n+      \"emcee\": [\"\"],\n+      \"hankel\": [\"\"],\n+      \"meshio\": [\"\"],\n+      \"numpy\": [\"\"],\n+      \"pyevtk\": [\"\"],\n+      \"scipy\": [\"\"],\n+      \"gstools-cython\": [\"\"]\n+    }\n+  },\n+  \"install_command\": [\n+    \"in-dir={env_dir} python {conf_dir}/benchmarks/tools/install_pyproject_extras.py --pyproject {conf_dir}/pyproject.toml rust\",\n+    \"in-dir={env_dir} python -m pip install --no-deps {build_dir}\"\n+  ],\n+  \"number\": 1,\n+  \"repeat\": 20\n+}\n+```\n+\n+Important details:\n+\n+- `environment_type: \"conda\"` means conda is required for the ASV workflow in\n+  this guide. ASV creates isolated conda environments for the commits it\n+  benchmarks.\n+- `pythons: [\"3.14\"]` means ASV creates Python 3.14 benchmark environments.\n+  Both ASV configs use Python 3.14 by default; change `pythons` in\n+  `asv.conf.json` and `asv.openmp.conf.json` only when intentionally\n+  validating another Python/GSTools backend stack.\n+- `number: 1` means ASV runs the benchmark code once per iteration.\n+- `repeat: 20` means the default baseline records 20 independent measurements\n+  per benchmark case.\n+- `matrix.req` asks ASV to install GSTools runtime dependencies before\n+  installing the checked-out GSTools source. It includes `gstools-cython`\n+  explicitly because the GSTools commit is installed with `--no-deps`.\n+- `{build_dir}` is ASV's temporary checkout/build directory for the exact\n+  GSTools commit being benchmarked.\n+- `install_command` installs the checked-out GSTools revision with `--no-deps`.\n+  It also uses `install_pyproject_extras.py` to install the `rust` extra from\n+  `pyproject.toml`, keeping the `gstools_core` requirement in one place.\n+- ASV still needs its own `install_command` because it creates isolated\n+  environments for the commits it benchmarks.\n+- Run the cProfile helper with the Python executable from ASV's isolated\n+  environment, for example `.asv/env/<env-id>/bin/python`. In that mode, the\n+  ASV environment provides dependencies while the helper imports the current\n+  checkout through the repo `src/` path.\n+\n+ASV creates these generated directories:\n+\n+```text\n+.asv/env/      benchmark environments\n+.asv/results/  local benchmark result JSON files\n+.asv/html/     generated local benchmark website\n+```\n+\n+Those directories are machine-specific generated artifacts. They should\n+normally stay out of git.\n+\n+If needed, users can list more than one branch, Python version, benchmark\n+directory, and so on. For example:\n+\n+```json\n+\"branches\": [\"main\", \"my-feature-branch\"]\n+```\n+\n+Users can also benchmark any explicit branch, commit, tag, or range without\n+changing `asv.conf.json`:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv run 'my-feature-branch^!' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+asv run main..my-feature-branch --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+```\n+\n+ASV checks out package code at each git commit being benchmarked. Commit source\n+changes before benchmarking them with ASV. Otherwise ASV may benchmark the last\n+committed package code rather than your uncommitted source changes.\n+\n+### Benchmark Naming\n+\n+ASV recognizes benchmark methods by name:\n+\n+- methods starting with `time_` measure runtime\n+- methods starting with `peakmem_` measure peak memory\n+- `setup_cache()` creates reusable data once per benchmark environment\n+- `setup()` can skip or prepare individual parameter combinations\n+\n+## Benchmark Coverage\n+\n+This section describes what is measured by the ASV suite and how the benchmark\n+labels map to real GSTools workflows. The goal is to cover representative\n+operations that are relevant for geostatistical work, not isolated\n+micro-functions.\n+\n+The current suite measures runtime and peak memory for variogram estimation,\n+global kriging, spatial random field generation, and conditioned random field\n+generation. Each workflow is run with both backends so the results can show\n+both absolute performance and Rust-vs-Cython differences.\n+\n+### Shared Constants\n+\n+```python\n+BACKENDS = (\"cython_fallback\", \"rust_core\")\n+THREAD_COUNTS = _configured_thread_counts()\n+VARIOGRAM_CASES = (\n+    \"full_900\",\n+    \"sampled_5000_to_1500\",\n+    \"sampled_15000_to_4500\",\n+)\n+KRIGE_CASES = (\"small_30x500\", \"large_120x2000\", \"extra_large_360x6000\")\n+FIELD_CASES = (\n+    \"srf_unstructured_randmeth\",\n+    \"srf_structured_randmeth\",\n+    \"srf_structured_fourier\",\n+    \"condsrf_unstructured\",\n+)\n+```\n+\n+These constants define backend parameter values and the case/thread labels used\n+in generated benchmark method names.\n+\n+`BACKENDS` compares:\n+\n+- `cython_fallback`\n+- `rust_core`\n+\n+`THREAD_COUNTS` defaults to:\n+\n+- `threads_1`: force `gstools.config.NUM_THREADS = 1`\n+\n+That is the default because the first benchmark target is a clean\n+Cython-vs-Rust backend comparison without parallelism.\n+\n+### Shared Helpers\n+\n+`gstools_backend(use_core, num_threads)` temporarily forces GSTools to use\n+either the Cython fallback backend or the Rust `gstools_core` backend, and\n+sets `gstools.config.NUM_THREADS` for that benchmark run.\n+\n+`_random_points(seed, count, scale)` creates deterministic 2D point clouds.\n+\n+`_smooth_field(x, y)` creates deterministic synthetic values:\n+\n+```python\n+np.sin(x / 10.0) + np.cos(y / 15.0)\n+```\n+\n+`_make_variogram_data(...)` creates positions, field values, and bins for\n+variogram estimation.\n+\n+`_make_krige_data(...)` creates conditioning points, conditioning values, and\n+target points for kriging and conditioned random fields.\n+\n+The fixed random seeds are intentional. They keep benchmark inputs stable so\n+changes in results are more likely to come from code changes, not new random\n+data.\n+\n+### Benchmark Classes\n+\n+The ASV benchmarking is organized around workflow classes. Each workflow class\n+compares `cython_fallback` and `rust_core`, and each class includes both\n+runtime and peak-memory methods.\n+\n+The suite currently measures:\n+\n+- `VariogramBenchmarks`: full pairwise work vs sampled large work\n+- `KrigingBenchmarks`: small vs larger global kriging systems\n+- `RandomFieldBenchmarks`: unstructured SRF, structured SRF, Fourier\n+  SRF, and conditioned SRF\n+\n+This keeps the ASV suite focused on representative workflows rather than\n+separate duplicate backend checks.\n+\n+#### VariogramBenchmarks\n+\n+This class measures variogram estimation cases:\n+\n+```text\n+full_900\n+sampled_5000_to_1500\n+sampled_15000_to_4500\n+```\n+\n+The labels mean:\n+\n+- `full_900`: create 900 scattered points and use all 900 points for the\n+  variogram calculation.\n+- `sampled_5000_to_1500`: create 5,000 scattered points, then randomly select\n+  1,500 of those points for the variogram calculation.\n+- `sampled_15000_to_4500`: create 15,000 scattered points, then randomly select\n+  4,500 of those points for the variogram calculation.\n+\n+The sampled cases still represent larger input datasets, but the variogram\n+calculation is done on the randomly selected subset so the pairwise work stays\n+practical.\n+\n+#### KrigingBenchmarks\n+\n+This class measures global kriging at three scales:\n+\n+```text\n+small_30x500\n+large_120x2000\n+extra_large_360x6000\n+```\n+\n+The labels mean:\n+\n+- `small_30x500`: 30 conditioning points, 500 target points\n+- `large_120x2000`: 120 conditioning points, 2,000 target points\n+- `extra_large_360x6000`: 360 conditioning points, 6,000 target points\n+\n+#### RandomFieldBenchmarks\n+\n+This class measures SRF and CondSRF generation workflows:\n+\n+```text\n+srf_unstructured_randmeth\n+srf_structured_randmeth\n+srf_structured_fourier\n+condsrf_unstructured\n+```\n+\n+The cases are:\n+\n+- `srf_unstructured_randmeth`: SRF using RandMeth on 2,000 unstructured points\n+- `srf_structured_randmeth`: SRF using RandMeth on a 64 by 64 structured grid\n+- `srf_structured_fourier`: SRF using the Fourier generator on a 64 by 64\n+  structured grid\n+- `condsrf_unstructured`: conditioned SRF with 40 conditioning points and 1,000\n+  target points\n+\n+## Running The Benchmarks\n+\n+### Baseline Benchmark\n+\n+The baseline benchmark is the first result set to create before doing any\n+optimization work. It uses the default ASV configuration, so each workflow is\n+measured with `threads_1` for both `cython_fallback` and `rust_core`.\n+\n+#### Main Branch Baseline\n+\n+- Save a baseline for the latest local `main` commit:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv run 'main^!' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+```\n+\n+#### Several Commits Baseline\n+\n+ASV can also compare several commits. This example runs the last three commits\n+on local `main`; choose a different range when that better matches your\n+branch.\n+\n+- Run the last three commits on the local `main` branch:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv run 'main~3..main' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+```\n+\n+#### Summary of Results\n+\n+After running ASV, inspect the explicit Rust-vs-Cython speedup ratios:\n+\n+```bash\n+python benchmarks/tools/asv_speedup_summary.py\n+```\n+\n+The helper reads `.asv/results/` and reports ratios per case and thread label:\n+\n+```text\n+speedup = cython_fallback_time / rust_core_time\n+```\n+\n+Interpret the ratio as:\n+\n+- `speedup > 1.0` means Rust is faster\n+- `speedup = 1.0` means similar performance\n+- `speedup < 1.0` means Rust is slower\n+\n+The speedup helper prints the backend ratio explicitly in the terminal. By\n+default, the helper skips removed legacy duplicate rows from older saved\n+results.\n+\n+For a report that is easier to paste into a PR or issue:\n+\n+```bash\n+python benchmarks/tools/asv_speedup_summary.py --format markdown\n+```\n+\n+For a small standalone HTML report:\n+\n+```bash\n+python benchmarks/tools/asv_speedup_summary.py --format html --output .asv/backend-report-overview.html\n+```\n+\n+#### Visualization of Results\n+\n+You can inspect the results in the ASV browser report by building and opening\n+the local website:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv publish\n+asv preview\n+```\n+\n+Then open the printed local URL, for example:\n+\n+```text\n+http://127.0.0.1:8080/#/\n+```\n+(or any other `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#/` URL shown by the running preview).\n+\n+The browser report shows raw ASV plots and trends. ASV plot views do not draw a\n+line when there is only one x-axis point, so a single-commit run such as\n+`asv run 'main^!' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics` may show results\n+without useful commit-trend graphs.\n+\n+### Profiling With cProfile\n+\n+`cProfile` does not update the ASV results shown in the browser report.\n+Instead, it prints a table in the terminal showing which Python\n+functions consumed time while one workflow ran.\n+\n+The helper script is:\n+\n+```text\n+benchmarks/tools/profile_benchmark_workflows.py\n+```\n+\n+It imports the ASV benchmark classes from `benchmark_two_point_statistics.py`,\n+selects one case, forces one backend, and runs that case under `cProfile`.\n+\n+Since ASV has already created an isolated Python environment, select that\n+environment to execute the profiling helper:\n+\n+```bash\n+ASV_ENV=\"$(ls -td .asv/env/* | head -n 1)\"\n+ASV_PYTHON=\"$ASV_ENV/bin/python\"\n+```\n+\n+On Windows PowerShell, use:\n+\n+```powershell\n+$asvEnv = Get-ChildItem .asv\\env -Directory |\n+  Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending |\n+  Select-Object -First 1\n+$asvPython = Join-Path $asvEnv.FullName 'python.exe'\n+```\n+\n+The helper still profiles the current checkout because\n+`profile_benchmark_workflows.py` adds the repository `src/` directory to\n+`sys.path`. The ASV environment provides the installed dependencies, including\n+`gstools-cython` and `gstools_core`.\n+\n+List available cases:\n+\n+```bash\n+\"$ASV_PYTHON\" benchmarks/tools/profile_benchmark_workflows.py --list\n+```\n+\n+On Windows PowerShell, replace `\"$ASV_PYTHON\"` with `& $asvPython`.\n+\n+Possible profile selected cases:\n+\n+```bash\n+\"$ASV_PYTHON\" benchmarks/tools/profile_benchmark_workflows.py --case variogram-sampled --backend rust_core --threads threads_1 --limit 10\n+\"$ASV_PYTHON\" benchmarks/tools/profile_benchmark_workflows.py --case variogram-extra-large --backend rust_core --threads threads_1 --limit 10\n+\"$ASV_PYTHON\" benchmarks/tools/profile_benchmark_workflows.py --case krige-large --backend rust_core --threads threads_1 --limit 10\n+\"$ASV_PYTHON\" benchmarks/tools/profile_benchmark_workflows.py --case krige-extra-large --backend rust_core --threads threads_1 --limit 10\n+\"$ASV_PYTHON\" benchmarks/tools/profile_benchmark_workflows.py --case condsrf --backend rust_core --threads threads_1 --limit 10\n+```\n+\n+## Optional Parallelization with OpenMP\n+\n+This section collects optional workflows for testing Cython and Rust with\n+several thread counts. OpenMP setup is platform-dependent, so each operating\n+system must be verified on the machine that produces the results.\n+\n+The default setup above remains the recommended baseline: one thread, normal\n+ASV environment, and no extra OpenMP build steps. Use this section only when\n+you explicitly want to measure backend scaling with multiple thread counts.\n+\n+### OpenMP ASV Configuration\n+\n+Use one OpenMP ASV config on all supported desktop platforms:\n+\n+```text\n+asv.openmp.conf.json\n+```\n+\n+This config keeps the OpenMP experiment separate from the default baseline:\n+\n+```text\n+.asv-openmp/env/\n+.asv-openmp/results/\n+.asv-openmp/html/\n+```\n+\n+It also uses fewer repeats than the baseline config:\n+\n+```json\n+\"number\": 1,\n+\"repeat\": 20\n+```\n+\n+That means each OpenMP benchmark case records 10 independent measurements by\n+default, while still running the benchmark code once per measurement.\n+\n+During ASV installation, it runs:\n+\n+```bash\n+benchmarks/tools/install_openmp_cython.py\n+```\n+\n+That helper compiles `gstools-cython` from source inside ASV's own\n+environment, not inside your active `gstools-benchmark` driver environment.\n+The helper sets `GSTOOLS_BUILD_PARALLEL=1` and then uses platform-specific\n+compiler handling:\n+\n+- macOS: uses Apple clang through wrapper scripts and conda's `llvm-openmp`.\n+- Linux: uses the ASV conda compiler toolchain when available.\n+- Windows: uses native MSVC Build Tools.\n+\n+### Run on macOS and Linux\n+\n+Use these commands from a POSIX shell on macOS or Linux. On macOS, install\n+Xcode command-line tools first. On Linux, make sure the conda compiler packages\n+from `asv.openmp.conf.json` solve for your platform.\n+\n+Create the ASV machine profile once:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv --config asv.openmp.conf.json machine --yes\n+```\n+\n+#### Verify Parallel Backends\n+\n+Only interpret the Cython rows as OpenMP-enabled, and the Rust rows as\n+parallel-ready, after this check passes inside the `.asv-openmp/env/...`\n+environment.\n+\n+On macOS and Linux:\n+\n+```bash\n+ASV_OPENMP_ENV=\"$(ls -td .asv-openmp/env/* | head -n 1)\"\n+\"$ASV_OPENMP_ENV/bin/python\" benchmarks/tools/check_backend_parallel_ready.py --verbose\n+```\n+\n+On Windows PowerShell:\n+\n+```powershell\n+$asvOpenmpEnv = Get-ChildItem .asv-openmp\\env -Directory |\n+  Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending |\n+  Select-Object -First 1\n+$asvOpenmpPython = Join-Path $asvOpenmpEnv.FullName 'python.exe'\n+& $asvOpenmpPython benchmarks\\tools\\check_backend_parallel_ready.py --verbose\n+```\n+\n+Expected passing output contains:\n+\n+```text\n+Cython OpenMP readiness: PASS\n+Rust backend readiness: PASS with NUM_THREADS=2\n+```\n+\n+If the check passes, run the last five commits:\n+\n+```bash\n+GSTOOLS_BENCHMARK_THREADS=1,2,4,8 \\\n+asv --config asv.openmp.conf.json run 'main~5..main' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics --show-stderr\n+```\n+\n+Print Rust-vs-Cython ratios from the OpenMP result folder:\n+\n+```bash\n+python benchmarks/tools/asv_speedup_summary.py --results-dir .asv-openmp/results\n+```\n+\n+Build a curated OpenMP HTML report:\n+\n+```bash\n+python benchmarks/tools/asv_speedup_summary.py \\\n+  --results-dir .asv-openmp/results \\\n+  --format html \\\n+  --output .asv-openmp/backend-report-openmp-overview.html\n+```\n+\n+Build the case/backend comparison report:\n+\n+```bash\n+python benchmarks/tools/plot_case_backend_comparison.py \\\n+  --results-dir .asv-openmp/results \\\n+  --max-commits 50 \\\n+  --output .asv-openmp/case-backend-comparison.html\n+```\n+\n+By default this report includes both time and peak-memory benchmarks. Use\n+`--metric time` or `--metric memory` when you want only one metric.\n+`--max-commits` limits only the generated custom report; it does not delete\n+raw ASV results.\n+\n+Build and preview the OpenMP browser report:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv --config asv.openmp.conf.json publish\n+asv --config asv.openmp.conf.json preview\n+```\n+\n+### Automated OpenMP Benchmarking\n+\n+The GitHub Actions benchmark workflow is split into three responsibilities:\n+\n+- `.github/workflows/asv-benchmarks.yml` keeps the fast cross-platform smoke\n+  and parallel-readiness checks.\n+- `.github/workflows/asv-openmp-pr.yml` runs the full Linux OpenMP comparison\n+  for benchmark-relevant pull requests. It benchmarks only the PR base and\n+  head commits, uploads the custom report and native ASV site as an artifact,\n+  and exposes the `OpenMP benchmark gate` required check.\n+- `.github/workflows/asv-openmp-publish.yml` runs only for trusted pushes to\n+  `jeilealr/GSTools:main`. It benchmarks the newly accepted commit, restores\n+  prior results, and publishes the cumulative history to\n+  `jeilealr/gstools-benchmarks-asv`.\n+\n+Both full workflows use Python 3.14, the stable ASV machine name\n+`github-actions-ubuntu`, and:\n+\n+```text\n+GSTOOLS_BENCHMARK_THREADS=1,2,4,8\n+```\n+\n+The published benchmark repository serves:\n+\n+```text\n+/          custom case/backend report for the latest 50 accepted commits\n+/asv/      complete native ASV OpenMP history\n+/results/  cumulative raw ASV result JSON\n+```\n+\n+GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner hardware can change. Use the machine\n+metadata displayed in the custom report when interpreting long-term results.\n+A stable self-hosted runner is preferable if absolute performance comparisons\n+become a release requirement.\n+\n+Before opening a PR, compare the latest local `main` commit with the current\n+branch without rerunning an arbitrary history window:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv --config asv.openmp.conf.json machine --yes\n+git rev-parse main HEAD > /tmp/gstools-asv-pr-commits.txt\n+\n+GSTOOLS_BENCHMARK_THREADS=1,2,4,8 \\\n+asv --config asv.openmp.conf.json run \\\n+  HASHFILE:/tmp/gstools-asv-pr-commits.txt \\\n+  --interleave-rounds \\\n+  --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics \\\n+  --show-stderr\n+```\n+\n+#### Benchmark Publishing Repository Setup\n+\n+Create `jeilealr/gstools-benchmarks-asv` as a public repository with an initial\n+`README.md`. In that repository, open **Settings > Pages**, select **Deploy\n+from a branch**, choose `main` and `/(root)`, then save.\n+\n+Create the restricted publishing credential from the GitHub profile settings:\n+\n+1. Open **Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens >\n+   Fine-grained tokens**.\n+2. Generate a token named `GSTools benchmark publisher` with a 90-day\n+   expiration.\n+3. Select resource owner `jeilealr` and grant access only to\n+   `gstools-benchmarks-asv`.\n+4. Set repository permission **Contents** to **Read and write**. Leave every\n+   other configurable permission at **No access**.\n+5. Copy the token once. Never put it in source files, chat, or workflow logs.\n+6. In `jeilealr/GSTools`, open **Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions**\n+   and create the repository secret `BENCHMARKS_REPO_TOKEN`.\n+\n+The secret is used only by the trusted publishing workflow. Pull-request\n+workflows, including workflows from forks, never receive it. Rotate the token\n+before its 90-day expiration.\n+\n+After the PR workflow has run once, protect `main` in `jeilealr/GSTools` and\n+require the `OpenMP benchmark gate` status check. Require the gate rather than\n+the conditional `Full OpenMP comparison on Linux` job so pull requests without\n+benchmark-relevant changes can still merge.\n+\n+### Run on Windows\n+\n+Use native Windows, not WSL, when you want Windows benchmark results. Install\n+Microsoft C++ Build Tools first, including the C++ build tools workload and a\n+Windows SDK. Run the commands from PowerShell or Anaconda Prompt after\n+activating the `gstools-benchmark` conda environment.\n+\n+Create the ASV machine profile once:\n+\n+```powershell\n+asv --config asv.openmp.conf.json machine --yes\n+```\n+\n+Run a quick OpenMP smoke run for the latest local `main` commit:\n+\n+```powershell\n+$env:GSTOOLS_BENCHMARK_THREADS = '1,2,4,8'\n+asv --config asv.openmp.conf.json run 'main^!' --quick --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics --show-stderr\n+```\n+\n+Verify the parallel backends with the PowerShell commands in\n+[Verify Parallel Backends](#verify-parallel-backends). If the check passes,\n+run the last five commits:\n+\n+```powershell\n+$env:GSTOOLS_BENCHMARK_THREADS = '1,2,4,8'\n+asv --config asv.openmp.conf.json run 'main~5..main' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics --show-stderr\n+```\n+\n+Print Rust-vs-Cython ratios from the OpenMP result folder:\n+\n+```powershell\n+python benchmarks\\tools\\asv_speedup_summary.py --results-dir .asv-openmp\\results\n+```\n+\n+Build a curated OpenMP HTML report:\n+\n+```powershell\n+python benchmarks\\tools\\asv_speedup_summary.py `\n+  --results-dir .asv-openmp\\results `\n+  --format html `\n+  --output .asv-openmp\\backend-report-openmp-overview.html\n+```\n+\n+Build the case/backend comparison report:\n+\n+```powershell\n+python benchmarks\\tools\\plot_case_backend_comparison.py `\n+  --results-dir .asv-openmp\\results `\n+  --output .asv-openmp\\case-backend-comparison.html\n+```\n+\n+By default this report includes both time and peak-memory benchmarks. Use\n+`--metric time` or `--metric memory` when you want only one metric.\n+\n+Build and preview the OpenMP browser report:\n+\n+```powershell\n+asv --config asv.openmp.conf.json publish\n+asv --config asv.openmp.conf.json preview\n+```\n+\n+When finished, clear the thread-count override if the PowerShell session will\n+be reused:\n+\n+```powershell\n+Remove-Item Env:\\GSTOOLS_BENCHMARK_THREADS\n+```\n+\n+### OpenMP Thread Rule\n+\n+The `GSTOOLS_BENCHMARK_THREADS=1,2,4,8` setting only tells the benchmark code to\n+run the same workflows with different `gstools.config.NUM_THREADS` values. It\n+does not, by itself, make the Cython backend parallel.\n+\n+For Cython OpenMP scaling, `gstools-cython` must be compiled with OpenMP inside\n+the same `.asv-openmp/env/...` environment that runs the benchmark. The\n+`asv.openmp.conf.json` install command does that through\n+`benchmarks/tools/install_openmp_cython.py`; the commands in\n+[Verify Parallel Backends](#verify-parallel-backends) are the proof that the\n+environment is ready. If that check fails, the benchmark may still run, but the\n+Cython rows should not be interpreted as OpenMP-enabled Cython results.\n+\n+### HPC Notes\n+\n+The `asv.openmp.conf.json` workflow is intended for local macOS, Linux, and\n+native Windows machines. Managed HPC systems often use custom compiler modules,\n+MPI/OpenMP runtimes, scheduler pinning, and CPU affinity rules. Use the same\n+validation rule there: only interpret Cython as OpenMP-enabled if\n+`check_backend_parallel_ready.py --verbose` passes inside the exact ASV\n+environment used for the benchmark run.\n+\n+### Profiling With cProfile for Multiple Threads\n+\n+To profile how a workflow changes across configured thread counts, run the\n+same cProfile case several times with the OpenMP ASV environment:\n+\n+```bash\n+ASV_OPENMP_ENV=\"$(ls -td .asv-openmp/env/* | head -n 1)\"\n+ASV_OPENMP_PYTHON=\"$ASV_OPENMP_ENV/bin/python\"\n+\n+for threads in threads_1 threads_2 threads_4 threads_8; do\n+  \"$ASV_OPENMP_PYTHON\" benchmarks/tools/profile_benchmark_workflows.py --case krige-extra-large --backend rust_core --threads \"$threads\" --limit 10\n+done\n+```\n+\n+On Windows PowerShell:\n+\n+```powershell\n+$asvOpenmpEnv = Get-ChildItem .asv-openmp\\env -Directory |\n+  Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending |\n+  Select-Object -First 1\n+$asvOpenmpPython = Join-Path $asvOpenmpEnv.FullName 'python.exe'\n+\n+foreach ($threads in 'threads_1', 'threads_2', 'threads_4', 'threads_8') {\n+  & $asvOpenmpPython benchmarks\\tools\\profile_benchmark_workflows.py --case krige-extra-large --backend rust_core --threads $threads --limit 10\n+}\n+```\n+\n+Useful options:\n+\n+- `--case`: choose one workflow, or use `all`\n+- `--backend`: choose `cython_fallback` or `rust_core`\n+- `--threads`: choose `threads_1` for a baseline profile, or `threads_2`,\n+  `threads_4`, or `threads_8` for parallel profiles\n+- `--limit`: number of function rows to print from the cProfile table\n+- `--sort cumtime`: sort by cumulative time, usually the best first view\n+- `--sort tottime`: sort by time spent directly in each function\n+- `--repeat`: repeat a workflow inside the profiler\n+\n+For example, `--limit 10` means \"print the top 10 function rows after sorting\".\n+\n+## More ASV Commands\n+\n+Save results for only the latest local `main` commit:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv run 'main^!' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+```\n+\n+Compare the latest local `main` commit with the previous local `main` commit:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv run 'main~1^!' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+asv run 'main^!' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+asv compare main~1 main\n+```\n+\n+Compare local `main` with the latest remote `main`:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv run 'main^!' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+git fetch origin main\n+asv run 'origin/main^!' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+asv compare origin/main main\n+```\n+\n+Compare the previous local `main` commit with the latest remote `main`:\n+\n+```bash\n+git fetch origin main\n+asv run 'main~1^!' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+asv run 'origin/main^!' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+asv compare main~1 origin/main\n+```\n+\n+Run the last three commits on local `main`:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv run 'main~3..main' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics --show-stderr\n+```\n+\n+Run the last three commits on the latest remote `main`:\n+\n+```bash\n+git fetch origin main\n+asv run 'origin/main~3..origin/main' --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics --show-stderr\n+```\n+\n+On a linear branch, `main~5..main` benchmarks:\n+\n+```text\n+main~4\n+main~3\n+main~2\n+main~1\n+main\n+```\n+\n+Run a selected list of commits:\n+\n+```bash\n+git rev-parse main main~3 origin/main e20c88f7 > /tmp/gstools-asv-commits.txt\n+asv run HASHFILE:/tmp/gstools-asv-commits.txt --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+```\n+\n+Use full commit hashes when sharing results. Short hashes and branch names are\n+fine locally but can become ambiguous later.\n+\n+If running ASV from outside the repo root, pass the config explicitly:\n+\n+```bash\n+asv --config /path/to/MPS-Tools/GSTools/asv.conf.json run --quick --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+```\n+\n+## External Reference\n+\n+For complete ASV command syntax, see:\n+\n+```text\n+https://asv.readthedocs.io/en/stable/commands.html\n+```\n@@ -0,0 +1 @@\n+\"\"\"ASV benchmark package for GSTools workflow performance checks.\"\"\"\n@@ -0,0 +1,375 @@\n+\"\"\"Benchmark representative two-point statistics workflows.\n+\n+Usage:\n+    cd /path/to/MPS-Tools/GSTools\n+    # See benchmarks/README.md for ASV and optional cProfile setup.\n+    asv machine --yes\n+    asv run --quick --show-stderr --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+    asv run main^! --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics\n+    asv run\n+    asv publish\n+    asv preview\n+    asv compare main~1 main\n+\n+Backend speedup should be interpreted as:\n+    speedup = cython_fallback_time / rust_core_time\n+\n+Values greater than 1.0 mean the Rust backend is faster on the same machine\n+for the same benchmark, case, commit, and thread count.\n+\n+By default the suite uses one GSTools thread. if item.startswith(\"threads_\"):\n+            value = item.removeprefix(\"threads_\")\n+        else:\n+            value = item\n+        thread_counts.append(int(value))\n+    if not krige_store=False,\n+        )\n@@ -0,0 +1,573 @@\n+#!/usr/bin/env python\n+\"\"\"Summarize Rust-vs-Cython speedups from local ASV result files.\n+\n+The summary is optional. ASV itself remains the source of truth for benchmark\n+storage and visualization. The helper understands both current generated\n+benchmark method names, which encode case and thread labels, and older\n+parameterized ASV result files.\n+\n+Usage:\n+    python benchmarks/tools/asv_speedup_summary.py\n+    python benchmarks/tools/asv_speedup_summary.py --results-dir .asv/results\n+    python benchmarks/tools/asv_speedup_summary.py --format markdown\n+    python benchmarks/tools/asv_speedup_summary.py --format html --output report.html\n+    python benchmarks/tools/asv_speedup_summary.py --include-legacy\n+\n+Speedup is calculated as:\n+    cython_fallback_time / rust_core_time\n+\n+Values greater than 1.0 mean Rust was faster on the same machine, commit,\n+environment, benchmark, case, and thread-count combination.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import argparse\n+import html\n+import itertools\n+import json\n+import math\n+import re\n+from datetime import datetime, timezone\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+BACKENDS = (\"cython_fallback\", \"rust_core\")\n+THREAD_PREFIX = \"threads_\"\n+BENCHMARK_PREFIXES = (\n+    \"time_variogram_estimate\",\n+    \"peakmem_variogram_estimate\",\n+    \"time_global_krige\",\n+    \"peakmem_global_krige\",\n+    \"time_field_generation\",\n+    \"peakmem_field_generation\",\n+)\n+LEGACY_BENCHMARKS = {\n+    \"time_srf\",\n+    \"peakmem_srf\",\n+    \"time_variogram\",\n+    \"peakmem_variogram\",\n+    \"time_krige\",\n+    \"peakmem_krige\",\n+}\n+\n+\n+def parse_args():\n+    \"\"\"Parse command-line options.\"\"\"\n+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n+        description=__doc__,\n+        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,\n+    )\n+    parser.add_argument(\n+        \"--results-dir\",\n+        default=None,\n+        action=\"append\",\n+        type=Path,\n+        help=(\n+            \"Path to an ASV results directory. It does not install the project or\n+its regular dependencies, so ASV can keep control of its environment matrix.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+import argparse\n+import subprocess\n+import sys\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+try:\n+    import tomllib\n+except ModuleNotFoundError:  # pragma: no cover - used on Python 3.8-3.10\n+    import tomli as tomllib\n+\n+\n+def parse_args():\n+    \"\"\"Parse command-line options.\"\"\"\n+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n+    parser.add_argument(\n+        \"extras\",\n+        nargs=\"+\",\n+        help=\"Optional dependency extras to install.\",\n+    )\n+    parser.add_argument(\n+        \"--pyproject\",\n+        type=Path,\n+        default=Path(\"pyproject.toml\"),\n+        help=\"Path to pyproject.toml. rows.append(\n+            {\n+                \"benchmark\": base_name,\n+                \"family\": family_from_name(base_name),\n+                \"metric\": metric_from_name(base_name),\n+ \"main\"\n+\n+permissions:\n+  contents: read\n+\n+concurrency:\n+  group: openmp-pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}\n+  cancel-in-progress: true\n+\n+env:\n+  ASV_CONFIG: asv.openmp.conf.json\n+  MACHINE_NAME: github-actions-ubuntu\n+\n+jobs:\n+  benchmark_changes:\n+    name: Detect benchmark-relevant changes\n+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n+    outputs:\n+      required: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.required }}\n+\n+    steps:\n+      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0\n+        with:\n+          fetch-depth: 0\n+\n+      - name: Detect benchmark-relevant changes\n+        id: changes\n+        env:\n+          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}\n+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}\n+        run: |\n+          if git diff --quiet \"$BASE_SHA\" \"$HEAD_SHA\" -- \\\n+            src \\\n+            benchmarks \\\n+            pyproject.toml \\\n+            asv.conf.json \\\n+            asv.openmp.conf.json \\\n+            .github/workflows/asv-benchmarks.yml \\\n+            .github/workflows/asv-openmp-pr.yml \\\n+            .github/workflows/asv-openmp-publish.yml\n+          then\n+            echo \"required=false\" >> \"$GITHUB_OUTPUT\"\n+          else\n+            echo \"required=true\" >> \"$GITHUB_OUTPUT\"\n+          fi\n+\n+  benchmark:\n+    name: Full OpenMP comparison on Linux\n+    if: needs.benchmark_changes.outputs.required == 'true'\n+    needs: benchmark_changes\n+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n+    timeout-minutes: 360\n+\n+    defaults:\n+      run:\n+        shell: bash -el {0}\n+\n+    steps:\n+      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0\n+        with:\n+          fetch-depth: 0\n+\n+      - uses: conda-incubator/setup-miniconda@fc2d68f6413eb2d87b895e92f8584b5b94a10167 # v3\n+        with:\n+          activate-environment: gstools-asv-driver\n+          python-version: \"3.14\"\n+          channels: conda-forge\n+          conda-remove-defaults: true\n+\n+      - name: Install ASV driver\n+        run: python -m pip install --upgrade pip asv\n+\n+      - name: Configure PR commits and ASV branches\n+        env:\n+          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}\n+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}\n+        run: |\n+          printf '%s\\n%s\\n' \"$BASE_SHA\" \"$HEAD_SHA\" \\\n+            > \"$RUNNER_TEMP/asv-pr-commits.txt\"\n+          python - <<'PY'\n+          import json\n+          import os\n+          from pathlib import Path\n+\n+          config = json.loads(Path(\"asv.openmp.conf.json\").read_text())\n+          config[\"branches\"] = [os.environ[\"BASE_SHA\"], os.environ[\"HEAD_SHA\"]]\n+          Path(\"asv.openmp.pr.conf.json\").write_text(\n+              json.dumps(config, indent=2),\n+              encoding=\"utf8\",\n+          )\n+          PY\n+          echo \"ASV_CONFIG=asv.openmp.pr.conf.json\" >> \"$GITHUB_ENV\"\n+\n+      - name: Configure stable ASV machine name\n+        run: |\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" machine \\\n+            --machine \"$MACHINE_NAME\" \\\n+            --yes\n+\n+      - name: Run full OpenMP comparison\n+        env:\n+          GSTOOLS_BENCHMARK_THREADS: \"1,2,4,8\"\n+        run: |\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" run \\\n+            \"HASHFILE:$RUNNER_TEMP/asv-pr-commits.txt\" \\\n+            --machine \"$MACHINE_NAME\" \\\n+            --interleave-rounds \\\n+            --no-pull \\\n+            --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics \\\n+            --show-stderr\n+\n+      - name: Write informational ASV comparison\n+        env:\n+          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}\n+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}\n+        run: |\n+          mkdir -p .asv-openmp/artifact\n+          set +e\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" compare \\\n+            \"$BASE_SHA\" \\\n+            \"$HEAD_SHA\" \\\n+            --machine \"$MACHINE_NAME\" \\\n+            --split \\\n+            | tee .asv-openmp/artifact/comparison.txt\n+          compare_status=\"${PIPESTATUS[0]}\"\n+          set -e\n+          echo \"ASV comparison exit status: $compare_status\" \\\n+            >> .asv-openmp/artifact/comparison.txt\n+\n+      - name: Build custom and native ASV reports\n+        run: |\n+          python benchmarks/tools/plot_case_backend_comparison.py \\\n+            --results-dir .asv-openmp/results \\\n+            --max-commits 50 \\\n+            --output .asv-openmp/artifact/index.html\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" publish \\\n+            --no-pull \\\n+            --html-dir .asv-openmp/artifact/asv\n+          cp -R .asv-openmp/results .asv-openmp/artifact/results\n+\n+      - benchmark_changes\n+      - benchmark\n+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n+\n+    steps:\n+      - name: Check required benchmark result\n+        env:\n+          CHANGE_RESULT: ${{ needs.benchmark_changes.result }}\n+          BENCHMARK_REQUIRED: ${{ needs.benchmark_changes.outputs.required }}\n+          BENCHMARK_RESULT: ${{ needs.benchmark.result }}\n+        run: |\n+          if [[ \"$CHANGE_RESULT\" != \"success\" ]]; then\n+            echo \"Could not determine whether the benchmark is required.\"\n+            exit 1\n+          fi\n+          if [[ \"$BENCHMARK_REQUIRED\" == \"true\" \\\n+            && \"$BENCHMARK_RESULT\" != \"success\" ]]; then\n+            echo \"The required OpenMP benchmark did not complete successfully.\"\n+            exit 1\n+          fi\n+          if [[ \"$BENCHMARK_REQUIRED\" == \"true\" ]]; then\n+            echo \"The required OpenMP benchmark completed successfully.\"\n+          else\n+            echo \"No benchmark-relevant files changed.\"\n+          fi\n@@ -0,0 +1,118 @@\n+name: Publish OpenMP Benchmark History\n+\n+on:\n+  push:\n+    branches:\n+      - name: Restore cumulative ASV results\n+        run: |\n+          mkdir -p .asv-openmp/results\n+          if [[ -d benchmark-site/results ]]; then\n+            cp -R benchmark-site/results/. .asv-openmp/results/\n+          fi\n+\n+      - name: Configure stable ASV machine name\n+        run: |\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" machine \\\n+            --machine \"$MACHINE_NAME\" \\\n+            --yes\n+\n+      - name: Benchmark newly accepted main commit\n+        env:\n+          GSTOOLS_BENCHMARK_THREADS: \"1,2,4,8\"\n+        run: |\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" run \\\n+            \"$GITHUB_SHA^!\" \\\n+            --machine \"$MACHINE_NAME\" \\\n+            --skip-existing-successful \\\n+            --no-pull \\\n+            --bench benchmark_two_point_statistics \\\n+            --show-stderr\n+\n+      - name: Build published reports and preserve raw results\n+        run: |\n+          rm -rf benchmark-site/asv benchmark-site/results\n+          python benchmarks/tools/plot_case_backend_comparison.py \\\n+            --results-dir .asv-openmp/results \\\n+            --max-commits 50 \\\n+            --output benchmark-site/index.html\n+          asv --config \"$ASV_CONFIG\" publish \\\n+            --no-pull \\\n+            --html-dir benchmark-site/asv\n+          cp -R .asv-openmp/results benchmark-site/results\n+          touch benchmark-site/.nojekyll\n+\n+      - name: Commit and push benchmark history\n+        working-directory: benchmark-site\n+        run: |\n+          git config user.name \"GSTools benchmark bot\"\n+          git config user.email \"actions@users.noreply.github.com\"\n+          git add -A\n+          if git diff --cached --quiet; then\n+            echo \"No benchmark history changes to publish.\"\n+            exit 0\n+          fi\n+          git commit -m \"Update OpenMP benchmarks for ${GITHUB_SHA::8}\"\n+          git push origin main\n@@ -41,6 +41,10 @@ htmlcov/\n .coverage\n .coverage.*\n .cache\n+.asv/*\n+.asv-openmp/*\n+.asv-ci/*\n+asv.ci.*.json\n nosetests.xml\n coverage.xml\n *.cover\n@@ -54,8 +54,8 @@ Install the package by typing the following command in a command terminal:\n \n     conda install gstools\n \n-In case conda forge is not set up for your system yet, see the easy to follow\n-instructions on [conda forge][conda_forge_link]. Airspeed Velocity ([ASV](https://github.com/airspeed-velocity/asv/)) benchmark suite for GSTools and a complementary profiling helper implemented with cProfile (part of the Python standard library).\n+\n+This guide benchmarks GSTools, inspects the\n+results, profiles where runtime is spent, and then decides what to optimize.\n+\n+Unit tests in `tests/` answer \"is the code correct?\". The ASV benchmarks in\n+`benchmarks/` answer \"how fast is this workflow, how much memory does it use,\n+and did that change across commits?\". The complementary cProfile helper\n+answers \"inside this workflow, which Python functions are taking most of the\n+time right now?\".\n+\n+The benchmarks compare two GSTools backends, which gives more context for\n+deciding where optimization work should go:\n+\n+- `cython_fallback`: the default Cython-backed fallback implementation from\n+  [gstools-cython](https://github.com/GeoStat-Framework/GSTools-Cython).\n+- `rust_core`: the Rust-backed implementation from\n+  [gstools_core](https://github.com/GeoStat-Framework/GSTools-Core).\n+\n+## Index\n+\n+- [Setup](#setup)\n+- [Benchmarking Scripts](#benchmarking-scripts)\n+  - [Benchmark Classes](#benchmark-classes)\n+    - [VariogramBenchmarks](#variogrambenchmarks)\n+    - [KrigingBenchmarks](#krigingbenchmarks)\n+    - [RandomFieldBenchmarks](#randomfieldbenchmarks)\n+- [Running The Benchmarks](#running-the-benchmarks)\n+  -
